norms.text: Every load taken gets a notched tally stick as its receipt.
Cargo is taken; the walker is let go.
The watch whistles when a walker rounds the bend.

taboos.text: Killing a walker, because his tribe then comes for the camp.
Taking a load without cutting its stick.

values.text: A robbed walker who comes back next season.
Cane lashed the same hour it is cut.

contempts.text: Raiders who kill on the tracks and leave the settled tribes to take the blame.

place.text: A blind bend over a pond: walkers are seen before they see the camp.

work.text: Cargo off the walked track, a stick for each load, hides smoked for trade.

trade.text: The best smoked hides are kept back for trade.

danger.text: A dead walker brings his tribe; the dens round the pond are a nuisance.

faction.text: No tribe owns the camp. The settled tribes take the blame for it.

rumour.text: Talk is of Cut-Rope's raiders on the same tracks.

directions.text: The track runs on to the Polers' Camp; the guides there pole on to Dead-Water Village.

addressTerms.text: Walker, for anyone on the track.
Guest, for one welcomed at the fire; ojel, for any outsider.

neverSaid.text: Who pays the camp to leave a stretch alone.

grievances.text: The settled tribes get blamed for the camp's work. Cut-Rope's killings get blamed on the camp.

rumours.text: The camp does not work some stretches of track this season. The lieutenant gives no reason.

dissent.text: He smokes the hides and keeps the best for trade; he is the camp's seller.
She holds the bend by day and knaps flint there; from it she has found walkers Cut-Rope killed on the same tracks. The camp gets the blame. She is right to worry.
